name: Active buzzer 5 V (TMB12A05)
description: Bare 12 mm magnetic active buzzer with a built-in oscillator: apply DC between + and - and it beeps at about 2.4 kHz (2400 ± 300 Hz, at least 95 dB at 10 cm at 5 V). Rated 5 V DC, works from 3 to 7 V; draws at most 30 mA (about 22 mA at 5 V, about 13 mA at 3.3 V per the datasheet's mA-V curve). No tone generation or PWM needed: + high = beep, low = silent. Sold as: Jiangsu Huawha (HNDZ) TMB12A05 active buzzer, 12 × 9.5 mm, two leads 7.6 mm apart: + (long lead, marked + on the top sticker) and -.
eli5: A little beeper with its own tone inside: give it power and it beeps, take it away and it goes quiet.

pins.description: Positive lead (longer leg, + on the sticker). High (3–7 V) = beep, low = silent. Driven straight from a 3.3 V GPIO it draws about 13 mA; for full 5 V volume switch it with an NPN transistor.
Negative lead, to ground (shared with the microcontroller)

buildNotes: Polarity matters: the longer lead (and the + on the sticker) goes to the GPIO or + supply, the shorter lead to GND. Reversed, it stays silent.
Active buzzer: it makes its own ~2.4 kHz tone from plain DC. Drive the pin high or low; PWM or tone() will not set the pitch and only makes it crackle. For melodies use a passive buzzer.

From a 3.3 V GPIO it draws about 13 mA and is somewhat quieter (about 87 dB vs 90 dB at 5 V). That is fine for an ESP32 pin; a Raspberry Pi Pico pin is rated for about 12 mA, so on a Pico (or for full volume) power + from 5 V and switch - to GND with an NPN transistor (e.g. 2N2222/S8050, 1 kΩ base resistor) — the transistor then makes a GPIO high = beep.
Never exceed 7 V on it; the datasheet's operating range is 3–7 V DC.
It is loud (95 dB at 10 cm). Leave the 'remove seal after washing' sticker on for a little less volume; peel it off for full volume after soldering.
The leads are 7.6 mm apart, so it straddles three breadboard holes; bend nothing, just skip the holes in between.

example.code:
from machine import Pin
import time

buzzer = Pin({_}, Pin.OUT, value=0)  # + high = beep (active buzzer)
while True:
    buzzer.value(1)
    print('BEEP ON')
    time.sleep(1)
    buzzer.value(0)
    print('BEEP OFF')
    time.sleep(2)

test.title: The buzzer switches on, then off again
